newsitem.title: CANADA: Westmin to sell Premier gold operations.
newsitem.headline: Westmin to sell Premier gold operations.

text.p: Westmin Resources Limited said on Wednesday that it decided to sell its Premier gold operations near Stewart, British Columbia along with a large package of nearby exploration properties.
The mining company said the move was part of its effort to focus on base metals. Midland Walwyn Capital Inc was hired to handle the sale.
The sale process will commence immediately with potential purchasers able to examine data in late February.
Westmin simultaneously announced an increase in reserves at Premier after a drilling program last year.
It said diluted proven and probable reserves totalled 386,000 tonnes with an uncut grade of 0.21 ounce per ton, 1.1 ounce silver per ton and 1.6 percent zinc.
These reserves were defined by partially testing the potential outlined in a resource evaluation study, completed a year ago.
That study inferred a reserve potential of 1,122,000 tons at a gold grade of 0.23 oz per ton, located in several target areas.

Westmin said it was significant that areas representing only a small portion of the tonnage identified in that study were tested by the 1996 drilling programs. The portion that was drill tested returned not only more than twice the projected tonnage of reserves but also a gold grade eight percent higher than expected.
The reserve expansion boosted hopes that Premier, which has been idled since December, would be able to restart soon.
Operations were suspended because of a lack of developed ore.

"The operation has a modern and efficient CIL milling facility and permitted tailings pond. Access to the reserves is good through extensive underground workings so that development capital required would be low," Westmin said.
The milling plant has capacity to process 2,000 tonnes of ore per day.
